lines.text: | N1 | What death is | Death is the breath gone | Psa 104:29; 1Ki 17:17 | |
| N2 | What death is | Death comes to everyone, and falls alike on those the world would set apart | Psa 89:48; Zec 1:5; Gen 3:22; Ecc 2:16; 3:2; Heb 9:27 | |
| N3 | What death is | The same death is met in different ways, and nothing goes with the dead | Job 21:23, 25; Psa 49:17; Pro 11:7 | |
| N4 | Death and sin | Scripture ties death to sin from the first command; Paul and James trace the movement from within | Gen 2:17; 3:4; Rom 5:12; 6:23; 7:5–10; Jam 1:15 | |
| N5 | Death and sin | Each person answers for his own sin; sin can be put away while a death still follows | Eze 18:4; 2Ki 14:6; 2Sa 12:13–14 | 2-1 (Eze 18:4, 20) |

| N6 | Death in the living | Scripture speaks of death inside a living person: the heart dying first, the living called dead, abiding in death | 1Sa 25:37–38; Col 2:13; Rev 3:1; 1Ti 5:6; 1Jo 3:14 | 8-4 (held) |
| N7 | Sleep and waking | Scripture's recurring picture for death is sleep, and its hope against death is waking | Job 14:12; 2Ki 4:31; Mat 9:24; Joh 11:13; 1Th 4:14 | |
| N8 | Sleep and waking | *I read*: the calls on God to wake speak from how it feels when God does not act | Psa 7:6; 35:23; 44:23; 59:4; 121:4 | |
| N9 | Sleep and waking | The waking of the dead is not the same for all | Dan 12:2; Isa 26:14, 19 | |

| N10 | Soul, spirit, heart | At death the soul departs, dies, is poured out, is named to the end, and has an end beyond death | Gen 35:18; Num 23:10; Isa 53:12; Num 19:11; Psa 49:15, 19 | 3-7 (widened) |
| N12 | Soul, spirit, heart | The spirit is committed and returns to God; where it goes, Ecc 3:21 leaves as a question | Psa 31:5; Luk 23:46; Act 7:59; Ecc 12:7; 3:21 | 2-15 |
| N13 | Soul, spirit, heart | No verse sends the soul one way and the spirit another | Psa 16:10; 49:15; Ecc 3:21; 12:7 | **3-9** |
| N14 | Soul, spirit, heart | The heart can die before the body; no verse speaks of the heart after death | 1Sa 25:37–38; Psa 31:12; Ecc 9:3 | |

| N16 | Delivered from death | Of 15 soul-delivered verses, 12 are a living person kept from dying; two look beyond death; one says no one can | Psa 116:3–8; 56:13; 30:3; 49:15; 16:10; 89:48 | **3-9** |
| N17 | Delivered from death | Death is pictured as something that surrounds and holds, with cords, snares and gates | 2Sa 22:5–6; Psa 9:13 | |
| N18 | Delivered from death | Deliverance from death is *for* something: walking before God and telling of him | Psa 56:13; 118:17; Job 33:26–30 | 2-3 (Jam 5:20) |
| N19 | After death | Scripture speaks of people alive before God after death, and uses both soul and spirit | Rev 6:9–10; Heb 12:23; 1Pe 3:19; Mat 10:28 | 3-10; 6-2 |
| N20 | After death | From this side of death, the dead are silent and gone | Job 14:10; Ecc 9:5; Psa 6:5; 115:17; 49:19 | |
| N21 | After death | With God, the dead are carried, blessed and at rest | Luk 16:22; Rev 14:13; 2Sa 12:23; Luk 20:38; 23:43; Php 1:23; 2Co 5:8 | |
- Jacob: "I shall go down to Sheol to my son, mourning" (Gen 37:35; also 42:38; 44:29, 31)
- "The wicked shall return to Sheol" (Psa 9:17); "Sheol … those who have sinned" (Job 24:19); 1Ki 2:6, 9
- Hezekiah: "I am consigned to the gates of Sheol for the rest of my years" (Isa 38:10)
- Job 17:13, 16 (Sheol as house and bed); Psa 141:7; Pro 5:5; 7:27; Pro 15:24
- Num 16:33; Psa 55:15; Pro 1:12 (down alive); Psa 31:17 ("go silently to Sheol")
- Nations and kings brought down: Isa 14:15; Eze 31:15–17; Mat 11:23; Luk 10:15
- Pro 27:20; 30:16 (never satisfied); Isa 28:18 (a covenant with death, an agreement with Sheol)
- Mat 16:18 ("the gates of hell shall not prevail")
- Rev 6:8 ("its rider's name was Death, and Hades followed him"); Rev 20:13 ("Death and Hades gave up the dead … and they were judged")
- Joh 11:11–12: "Our friend Lazarus has fallen asleep, but I go to awaken him"
- 1Co 15:6, 18; 1Th 4:13, 15 (those asleep; "that you may not grieve as others do who have no hope")
- 1Co 7:39; 11:30 (*koimaō* rendered "dies", "died")
- Psa 18:5 ("the cords of Sheol entangled me"; the narrative cites the 2Sa 22 parallel); Pro 23:14
oracle as Jer 51:39, which the narrative cites); Lev 13:11 ("chronic") and Lev 26:10 ("long kept"), where
H3462 is not *sleep*; Isa 7:11 and Job 11:8 (Sheol as a measure of depth); Isa 57:9.
